newsitem.title: USA: U.S. regulators ok CBOT-LIFFE trading link.
newsitem.headline: U.S. regulators ok CBOT-LIFFE trading link.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade and the London International Financial Futures Exchange will be permitted to list each other's biggest financial futures and options for trading, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Wednesday.
The Chicago and London exchanges will list each other's major financial futures and options for trading on its floor by open outcry during hours that the original exchange's trading floor is closed.
The plan also links the Board of Trade Clearing Corporations and the London Clearing House for execution of the trades.

The link means that traders will be able to establish a position in a LIFFE-designated contract at the CBOT that will be transferred to the London Clearing House on the same day and be recognized as a LIFFE position. The same thing will occur at the LIFFE with certain Chicago contracts.

The two exchanges want to eventually have the CBOT's long-term and short-term U.S. Treasury Note futures and options contracts introduced for trading in London, and contracts on LIFFE's long-term British Gilts and Italian Government Bonds on the Chicago floor.

To maintain the fungibility of contracts traded through the link, the CFTC said it would permit LIFFE-designated options executed in Chicago to be margined futures-style. That marks the first time the agency has permitted such treatment for options traded on a U.S. exchange.
